summary: Reconciles two validated stage-1 proposals in the math_and_collision scope into one conservative engine map. Three canonical families are carried forward largely as proposed: CollisionPrimitives (stateless geometry/vector math, GUESS shape-based grouping), SparseConstraintSolver (two standalone global-workspace LDLT kernels, DERIVED), and the wave_001 families MatrixVectorHelpers, PackedShortVectorRecord, PhysicsFrameTransform, EmbeddedArrayBlock. The single substantive merge: the CollisionModel container from proposal math_and_collision_01 and the SpatialNearestNeighborQuery family from wave_001 are merged, because 0x00403640 and 0x004038E0 independently land on the same container fields (strut count this+0x130, strut array base this+0x134, 316-byte stride) and 0x00403AA0 falls back into 0x004038E0 by call. Node-chain method 0x004039C0 joins on the shared +272 node-link concept, not container fields, and is flagged accordingly. All owners are UNKNOWN or descriptive at the function-IR level; no trust is promoted. Disagreements (element-width conflict in MatrixVectorHelpers, three distinct codec layouts, shape-only CollisionPrimitives grouping, one-vs-two solver kernels) are preserved in conflicts and unresolved rather than erased.

engine_subsystems.name: MathAndCollision
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Stateless geometry/vector math primitives (ray-sphere quadratic intersection feeding suspension force, 2D direction projection, SSE two-point interpolation); spatial nearest-neighbor queries over strut arrays, BVH node chains and spatial trees, and a collision-geometry container owning strut/struct arrays with a destructor-style teardown; matrix/vector helpers (3x3-by-vector multiply, Euler-to-matrix); compressed short-int vector codecs; a per-frame physics frame transform; a zero-init helper for embedded 16-dword array blocks; and two standalone sparse-matrix LDLT constraint solvers operating on global double workspaces.

canonical_type_families.name: CollisionPrimitives
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Stateless geometric/vector math primitives: ray-sphere quadratic intersection (suspension contact), 2D direction projection, and SSE two-point linear interpolation. No instance fields beyond the two sampled floats, no callees; grouped by shape only (owner identity not proven by the packet).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Two float field samples (+0x0 x, +0x8 z) are read by 0x00423AD0 only; they are boundary clues for a caller-side vector argument, not evidence of a shared instance layout. No further field entries are emitted. Element widths and the roles of the six doubles in 0x00401180 are inferred from call context only.

canonical_type_families.name: CollisionModel
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Collision-geometry container owning the strut array (base this+0x134, count this+0x130, 316-byte stride), a 28-byte-stride struct array at +0x154, and further owned buffers at +0x150/+0x158. Supports nearest-neighbor spatial queries over the strut array and linked node chains (0x00403640, 0x004038E0), a spatial-tree query that falls back into 0x004038E0 (0x00403AA0), a linked node-chain walk used by AI steering (0x004039C0), indexed struct reads (0x00403F70), and a destructor-style teardown freeing every owned allocation (0x004045F0). Merge of proposal CollisionModel (math_and_collision_01:1) and proposal SpatialNearestNeighborQuery (wave_001:0): both independently describe the same +0x130/+0x134 316-byte-stride strut container. Name is descriptive; the packet reports owner UNKNOWN.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Container fields are sampled: +0x130 strut_count (int32, read/write), +0x134 strut_array_base (pointer, read/write), +0x138 array_reset_state (int32, write only in teardown), +0x148 released_sentinel (float32, write), +0x150/+0x154/+0x158 owned pointer buffers (read/write; +0x154 also the struct-array base read by 0x00403F70). Query-input floats +0x0/+0x4/+0x8 are evidenced only by 0x004039C0 and belong to the chain-walk input, not the container. Read-only fields +0x1C8, +0x1CC, +0x1D0, +0x1D8, +0x1E0, +0x244, +0x260 evidenced by 0x004038E0 have unknown roles and are not named. Strut/node element layouts (position, plane coefficients, node links +0x110/+0x10C/+268/+272, type selector +0x12C/+300, path length +60, stride 316) are documented in proposal prose but have no allowed field:<base>:<offset> evidence refs, so no element field entries are emitted; treat element layouts as boundary clues only.

canonical_type_families.name: SparseConstraintSolver
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Standalone numeric kernels: block LDL^T factorization and substitution solve of sparse dynamics constraint matrices stored in global double workspaces (0x008CFBF0..0x008D3B60 and 0x008D2120..0x008D3978) indexed by global row-pointer arrays. Two independent functions grouped by shared algorithm and overlapping global workspace region; whether they are two phases of one solver, two instances, or two kernels is not provable from the packet.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No instance fields sampled; solver state lives entirely in global double workspaces and row-pointer tables (0x008D3988..0x008D3A24, 0x008D3B68..0x008D3BF0). No field entries are emitted. The region 0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 is touched by both functions and is treated as shared scratch, not as ownership evidence.

canonical_type_families.name: MatrixVectorHelpers
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Pure matrix/vector math: 3x3 matrix-by-vector multiply on nine doubles (row-major, this+0x0..0x40) and Euler-angle to rotation-matrix conversion (floats). Shared offsets 0x00-0x20 may hold distinct element widths; grouping is a DERIVED proposal, not proven common storage.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Thirteen field samples across +0x00..+0x40. Element widths conflict: 0x00435E00 reads 8-byte doubles at 8-byte stride (+0x00..+0x40) while 0x00566E40 writes 4-byte floats at 4-byte stride (+0x00..+0x20). Shared offsets 0x00-0x20 therefore may be distinct storage; samples are boundary clues and a single element type must not be assumed at shared offsets. 0x00566E40 input angles are read via pointer arithmetic, not the this-based field list.

canonical_type_families.name: PackedShortVectorRecord
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Compressed int16 vector codecs: unpack compact records into floats with documented scales (1/2048, 0.02, 1/512). The three methods read different record layouts; grouping is DERIVED and common ownership of a single record struct is unproven.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Eleven field samples over three distinct record layouts (+0x0..+0x10: three raw dwords plus three int16 at +0xC/+0xE/+0x10 scaled by 1/2048 via global 0x0059E77C; +0x1E/+0x20/+0x22 scaled by 0.02 via 0x0059E6EC; +0x28/+0x2A scaled by 1/512 via 0x0059E4D8 with the Y output zeroed). Each layout is a separate boundary clue; no single record struct is asserted. Scale globals are read, but the raw source inlines the scale literals.

canonical_type_families.name: PhysicsFrameTransform
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame vehicle physics transform setup: copy a 3x3 rotation matrix and an input 3-vector into a frame buffer at base+0x34B0, compute and store their matrix-by-vector product, and return a pointer to the stored matrix. Called per frame from VehiclePhysicsTimeStep.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Fifteen float samples, all write access from a single method: rotation matrix 3x3 at +0x34B0..+0x34D0, input vector +0x3534..+0x353C, output vector +0x3540..+0x3548. Treated as a frame-buffer layout region; the runtime role of the output vector within the physics step is not described in the packet.

canonical_type_families.name: EmbeddedArrayBlock
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Zero-initialized 16-dword embedded array block inside larger construction objects (physics defaults, tire model data). Returns the this pointer; no reads, globals, or callees.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Sixteen dword samples +0x00..+0x3C, all write access; a 16-element zero-init block embedded in larger construction objects. Element type unknown; samples are boundary clues for the embedded region only.

interfaces.name: ISpatialQuery
interfaces.purpose: Nearest-node / nearest-strut spatial lookup used by AI steering and racing-line code, with optional strut-type filtering and plane-side rejection.

interfaces.name: ICompressedVectorCodec
interfaces.purpose: Decode compact int16-packed position/direction records into float vectors on the per-frame physics and audio paths.

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionRaySphereContact
compatibility_contracts.description: Ray-sphere quadratic intersection used by the vehicle suspension force calculation: takes six doubles, returns 0.0 on any miss and 1/sqrt(p) as a penetration-length proxy on hit. Must remain a pure scalar float-returning function with no side effects or callees.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionModelOwnedBufferLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The collision container owns pointer buffers at +0x150/+0x154/+0x158 and a 316-byte-stride element array at +0x134 (count +0x130) whose allocation is length-prefixed 4 bytes before the base. Teardown frees each non-null buffer via FreeWrapper_7bcf, runs per-element release (0x004B0170) over the element array, frees the array allocation, nulls the pointers, writes -1.0f at +0x148, clears +0x130/+0x134/+0x138, and returns the prior array base.

compatibility_contracts.name: NearestNeighborQueryResult
compatibility_contracts.description: Nearest-neighbor query walks linked collision nodes (next pointers at +0x110/+0x10C) and the strut array (316-byte stride, entries with type field at +0x12C <= 1 distance-tested), using a signed plane-distance probe (0x004FB6D0). Returns a node pointer, preferring the plane-verified candidate when its final signed distance is non-negative.

compatibility_contracts.name: SparseConstraintSolverWorkspace
compatibility_contracts.description: Two standalone LDLT solvers factor global double constraint-matrix workspaces (0x008CFBF0..0x008D3B60 and 0x008D2120..0x008D3978) indexed by global row-pointer arrays (0x008D3988..0x008D3A24 and 0x008D3B68..0x008D3BF0); both take no parameters and return 0. A replacement must keep these global buffers and pointer tables byte-compatible.

compatibility_contracts.name: NearestNeighborQuerySemantics
compatibility_contracts.description: Nearest-neighbor lookups must preserve the documented selection rules: zero-count early return (strut count at base+0x130 <= 0), strut-type filter (a3 == -1 or equals element type at +300), plane-side rejection selecting the linked +272 child, and the 200.0 accumulated path-length bound for chain traversal.

compatibility_contracts.name: ShortVectorPackingScale
compatibility_contracts.description: Compressed int16 vectors must decode with the packet's documented scale factors: 1/2048 for the 3-dword + 3-int16 record, 0.02 for the this[15..17] record, and 1/512 for the 2-component this[20]/this[21] record with the Y output component zeroed.

compatibility_contracts.name: MatrixVectorMultiplyReturnsInput
compatibility_contracts.description: The 3x3-by-vector multiply must return the input vector pointer; the Euler conversion must produce a row-major 3x3 rotation matrix with no side effects; MatrixVectorSetup must return a pointer to the stored matrix.

conflicts.subject: CollisionModel vs SpatialNearestNeighborQuery strut container
alternatives: Keep the two proposals as distinct families; strut fields +0x130/+0x134 with stride 316 appearing in both 0x00403640 and 0x004038E0 would be coincidental offset sharing.
Merge: both functions are nearest-strut queries over the same container fields (count +0x130, base +0x134, stride 316), so the two proposals describe one collision-geometry container.
Partial merge: merge strut-query methods only, leaving the node-chain walk 0x004039C0 and tree walk 0x00403AA0 as a separate spatial-query family.
conflicts.resolution: Merged into a single CollisionModel canonical family on container-field identity plus role (both are plane-gated nearest-strut queries) and the 0x00403AA0 -> 0x004038E0 fallback call. 0x004039C0 is carried into the same family on the shared +272 node-link concept, not on container fields, and its membership is flagged by its separate +0/+4/+8 query-input field evidence.

conflicts.subject: MatrixVectorHelpers shared offsets 0x00-0x20 element width
alternatives: Single 3x3 storage block shared by the multiply and the Euler conversion.
Distinct storage: 0x00435E00 reads 8-byte doubles at 8-byte stride while 0x00566E40 writes 4-byte floats at 4-byte stride, so offsets 0x00-0x20 cannot host both element widths at once.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as one family; the element-width conflict is preserved in the field_policy. A layout engineer must not assume a single element type at the shared offsets; the grouping remains a DERIVED proposal, not proven common storage.

conflicts.subject: PackedShortVectorRecord single-record-struct assumption
alternatives: One record struct whose three methods decode different regions.
Three independent codec record types (+0x0..+0x10, +0x1E..+0x22, +0x28..+0x2A) with no shared storage.
conflicts.resolution: Kept grouped per both proposals; each method's layout is treated as its own boundary clue with its own scale global, and no single struct layout is asserted. Common ownership remains unproven.

conflicts.subject: CollisionPrimitives grouping (shape-only)
alternatives: One stateless primitives class grouping the three math helpers.
Three independent free functions whose owners are UNKNOWN; grouping proves no shared class.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as a GUESS family per the proposal; each method's owner remains UNKNOWN, no shared instance storage is assumed beyond the two sampled floats, and the three helpers serve unrelated call paths (suspension force, AI/opponent proximity, no callers).

conflicts.subject: SparseConstraintSolver one kernel vs two
alternatives: Two phases of one LDLT solver (e.g. factorization + solve).
Two solver instances over disjoint matrix buffers.
Two independent standalone kernels that merely overlap global scratch space 0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60.
conflicts.resolution: Recorded as unresolved; both functions are kept in one family on shared algorithm and overlapping workspace region, and the shared region is explicitly treated as scratch, not as ownership or sequencing evidence. Whether the final solve tail is backward substitution or an interleaved block-triangular solve remains open.

unresolved: CollisionPrimitives: owner identity is UNKNOWN at the function-IR level; grouping is by shape only. 0x00401180 serves the suspension path, 0x00423AD0 an AI/opponent proximity path, and 0x0051F6A0 has no callers; no shared class is proven.
CollisionModel: the name is descriptive; the packet reports owner identity UNKNOWN. Field +0x138 is only observed being reset to 0 in teardown; its live role is unknown.

Strut/node element layouts (position, plane coefficients, node links +0x110/+0x10C/+268/+272, type selector +0x12C/+300, path length +60, stride 316) are documented in proposal prose but have no allowed field:<base>:<offset> evidence refs, so no element field entries are emitted. They remain boundary clues.

0x004039C0: query-position fields +0/+4/+8 are evidenced by this function only; whether node+272 is a child pointer or a sibling link is inferred, not provable from this packet alone; the meaning of the 200.0 bound (flt_59E470) as a search radius is DERIVED - the raw source only compares accumulated path length against it.
0x00403AA0: the function's own use of this-fields is not evidenced by packet operations; it is included in CollisionModel via its fallback call into 0x004038E0 only.
Fields this+0x1C8, +0x1CC, +0x1D0, +0x1D8, +0x1E0, +0x244, +0x260 are listed as read by 0x004038E0 but do not appear in the raw source text; their role is unknown.

0x00403640: meaning of read-only globals flt_59E440, flt_59E468, flt_59E46C not visible in raw source; the 4x-weighted Z component in the squared-distance score is unexplained.

0x0051F6A0: a5/a6 passed as unsigned ints and reinterpreted as floats via shuffle (type not determinable); only high halves of each double are used; no caller/callee evidence for what the two-point vectors encode.

0x0056FA96: exact role of workspace diagonals 0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 (RHS vector, D-factor, or solve accumulator) not decidable; whether the final tail is strictly backward substitution or an interleaved block-triangular solve is ambiguous; pointer tables 0x008D3988..0x008D3A24 point at runtime row bases not present in the packet; return 0 contract unconfirmed (no static callers).

0x00575BBD: pointer array 0x008D3B68..0x008D3BF0 holds runtime row bases outside this function; numeric immediates are absolute addresses encoded as 32-bit constants (equivalence to named globals is by address match only); block sizes DERIVED from loop bounds, not confirmed; LDL^T vs Cholesky interpretation DERIVED from the reciprocal-diagonal + rank-1-update pattern; exact forward/backward solve split not confirmed.

The two solver functions share overlapping global workspace region 0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 but operate on disjoint matrix buffers; whether they are two phases of one solver, two solver instances, or two independent kernels is not provable from the packet.

The role of the output vector written by 0x004F17D0 within the per-frame physics step is not described in the packet.

Callers known only through evidence refs (0x00401340, 0x00424790, 0x00424E70, 0x004270A0, 0x0042A7D0, 0x0042DA30, 0x004A5FA0, 0x004C6F10, 0x004C73F0, 0x004D1100, 0x004F2B50, 0x004F34E0, 0x004FF680); no caller-side packet data is available.
